definition_english: Characterizing a river, stream, spring, pond, or water-distribution system that maintains continuous liquid flow or standing water throughout all seasons of the year rather than drying out ephemerally.
definition_hindi: वर्ष की सभी ऋतुओं में निरंतर जल-प्रवाह अथवा स्थायी जल-संग्रह बनाए रखने वाली नदी, सरिता, झरने, ताल या जल-वितरण प्रणाली का विशेषण (जो मौसमी या अल्पकालिक रूप से सूखती नहीं है)।

hindi_equivalents_etymology.सदानीरा: Sanskrit tatsama compound सदा + नीर + -आ (sadā + nīra + -ā, 'always + water'), attested in Hindwi
hindi_equivalents_etymology.बारहमासी: Native Hindi compound बारह + मास (bārah + mās, 'twelve + months'), attested in Hindi Shabdasagar Part 5, p. 147
hindi_equivalents_etymology.चिरस्थायी: Sanskrit tatsama compound चिर + स्थायी (cira + sthāyī, 'long-lasting + standing/enduring'), attested in Hindwi

related_concepts: bamboo drip irrigation from perennial springs

equivalence_mapping.usage_status: Directly attested in NCERT Geography (सदानीरा झरनों), Hindwi, and Hindi Wiktionary Bhugol Shabdavali; root meaning ('always with water') restricts it specifically to hydrology
Directly attested in NCERT Geography (बारहमासी पेयजल) and Hindi Wiktionary Bhugol Shabdavali (बारहमासी सरिता, बारहमासी ताल); widely used in general geography and water resources
Recorded in Hindi Wiktionary Bhugol Shabdavali for standing water bodies (चिरस्थायी ताल for perennial pond)
Denotes year-round green foliage in botany (evergreen), not continuous water flow in rivers or springs

syntactic_patterns: attributive adjective before hydrological nouns (perennial river systems, perennial water bodies, perennial pond)
predicative adjective after copula (Is it perennial or ephemeral)

hindi.noun_type: व्यक्तिवाचक संज्ञा when used as river proper name (गण्डकी/करतोया); जातिवाचक संज्ञा head nouns in compounds (सरिता f., झरना m., पेयजल m., ताल m.)
hindi.gender: Invariable (अविकारी) in attributive adjectival use (e.g., सदानीरा झरनों); Feminine (स्त्रीलिंग) as standalone noun
hindi.number: Invariable (अविकारी) as adjective; modified head nouns inflect (झरना sg. -> झरनों pl. obl.)
hindi.case: Invariable across direct and oblique cases as adjective
hindi.declension: Indeclinable / Invariable in attributive adjectival use (अविकारी विशेषण); standalone noun ends in invariable feminine -आ
hindi.adjective_agreement: Invariable (अविकारी); feminine -आ ending of सदानीरा is neutralized in NCERT attributive use (सदानीरा झरनों की), where postposition की agrees with the following noun phrase rather than सदानीरा
syntactic_patterns: attributive pre-nominal modifier before masculine plural oblique or feminine singular hydrological nouns (सदानीरा झरनों की, बारहमासी सरिता, बारहमासी पेयजल, चिरस्थायी ताल)

register_and_pragmatics.academic_register: Geography, hydrology, and environmental textbook register (NCERT, Wiktionary Bhugol Shabdavali)
register_and_pragmatics.connotation: Elevated and classically resonant for सदानीरा; neutral and accessible for बारहमासी
cultural_nuances: सदानीरा functions in classical Sanskrit-Hindi literature and NCERT Sanskrit/Hindi notes as a proper name for the Gandaki (Narayani) and Karatoya rivers alongside its generic hydrological adjectival use.
usage_restrictions: Restrict सदानीरा strictly to water bodies, rivers, streams, and springs; never apply it to plants (S1), staff (S4), or abstract problems (S3).
Do not use सदाबहार (evergreen) for rivers or water systems.

linguistic_analysis.morphosyntax: Although Hindwi classifies सदानीरा as a feminine noun (स्त्रीलिंग संज्ञा), NCERT Class X Geography (जल संसाधन) deploys it as a morphologically invariable attributive adjective before a masculine plural oblique noun (सदानीरा झरनों की), demonstrating neutralization of feminine gender agreement in modern academic Hindi.
linguistic_analysis.collocational_distribution: बारहमासी combines freely with both flowing water (बारहमासी सरिता), potable supply (बारहमासी पेयजल), and standing water (बारहमासी ताल), whereas चिरस्थायी is specifically attested for standing ponds (चिरस्थायी ताल) in Wiktionary's Bhugol Shabdavali.

conceptual_analysis.core_distinction: Characterizes continuous year-round availability of liquid surface or spring water across dry and wet seasons, directly opposed to ephemeral (rain-fed/seasonal) watercourses in NCERT physical geography.
conceptual_analysis.domain_boundary: Restricted strictly to hydrology, fluvial geomorphology, and water-resource systems (S2); distinct from multi-year plant longevity (S1), recurring socio-historical problems (S3), permanent administrative staffing (S4), and timeless philosophical doctrines (S5).

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Both designate rivers, streams, springs, and water sources that retain water throughout all twelve months without drying up seasonally.
pairwise_comparison.difference: सदानीरा ('always containing water') is semantically specialized for hydrology and carries an elevated literary-geographical register, though it also serves as a proper name for the Gandaki and Karatoya rivers; बारहमासी ('twelve-monthly') is transparent, widely accessible across NCERT textbooks, and shared with botany (S1).
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: High for rivers, streams, and springs (e.g., सदानीरा/बारहमासी सरिता); prefer बारहमासी for potable water supply (बारहमासी पेयजल) and सदानीरा when emphasizing hydrological specificity.

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Both appear in Hindi Wiktionary's Bhugol Shabdavali for water bodies that persist without seasonal desiccation (बारहमासी ताल / चिरस्थायी ताल for perennial pond).
pairwise_comparison.difference: चिरस्थायी denotes general long-term durability across administration (S4) and physical phenomena (S3) rather than specifically hydrological water flow, making it suitable for standing ponds (ताल) but unnatural for flowing rivers or springs.
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: Limited to standing water bodies like ponds (ताल); not interchangeable for rivers, streams, or springs.

proposed_terminology.justification: Existing Hindi equivalents सदानीरा (for hydrological specificity in rivers, streams, and springs) and बारहमासी (for general water resources and drinking water) are well-established in NCERT textbooks; no new coinage is needed.

overall_confidence: Moderate-High — Hydrological sense S2 and its Hindi equivalents सदानीरा and बारहमासी are directly attested in NCERT Class X Geography (jhss103.pdf), Hindwi, and Hindi Wiktionary's Bhugol Shabdavali, though an explicit CSTT portal headword record remains unverified.
